title: Dragon Alchemist's Enchanted Brew
description: A miniature dragon perches on the rim of a giant coffee mug, breathing prismatic dispersion energy into the brew below. The user controls the dragon's breath intensity, mug liquid color, camera orbit, dispersion gem placement, lighting mood, and can trigger a magical eruption sequence — all through an interactive GUI panel.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads three GLB assets: coffeeMug.glb, DragonDispersion.glb, and DispersionTest.glb. Scene setup: Place the coffee mug at the world origin scaled appropriately to be the central object. Position the DragonDispersion model scaled down to roughly 30% of the mug height, perched on the mug's rim tilted slightly inward as if breathing into the cup. Place the DispersionTest model inside the mug, floating just above the mug's interior bottom, slowly rotating to simulate a magical gem submerged in the brew. Camera: Use OrbitControls with initial position at (0, 3, 5) looking at the mug center. Clamp polar angle between 10 and 80 degrees. Lighting: Add an ambient light (intensity 0.3), a directional light from above-right, and a point light inside the mug with color matching the brew that casts a soft glow upward. Add a lil-gui panel with these interactive controls: (1) 'Breath Intensity' slider (0.0-2.0) that scales a pulsing emissive glow on the dragon model and adjusts the inner point light intensity. (2) 'Brew Color' color picker that changes the point light color inside the mug and applies a tinted transparent MeshPhysicalMaterial plane hovering inside the mug to simulate liquid surface with transmission and roughness. (3) 'Gem Spin Speed' slider (0.0-5.0) controlling the DispersionTest rotation speed. (4) 'Gem Vertical Offset' slider (-0.5 to 1.0) to raise or lower the gem inside the mug. (5) 'Lighting Mood' dropdown with options 'Warm', 'Cool', 'Mystic' that changes the directional light color and ambient intensity. (6) 'Eruption' button that triggers a 3-second animation: the gem rapidly rises above the mug rim, the dragon emissive flashes white, particles (use Points with BufferGeometry, 200 vertices randomized in a cone shape) burst upward from the mug with the brew color, then everything settles back. Validate all slider parameters are clamped to their defined ranges. Use requestAnimationFrame for the render loop. Ensure all models load via GLTFLoader before rendering.
